extracted.intended_audience: museums and other eligible organizations applying for IMLS Museums for America grants (FY2024)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and review criteria for applicants to the IMLS Museums for America FY2024 grant program, including registration, allowable costs, required certifications, review criteria, and award administration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting materials (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibit design plans; Reports from planning activities; Contractor quotes; Equipment specifications; Products or evaluations from previously completed or ongoing projects of a similar nature; Collections, technology, or other departmental plans for the organization as applicable to the proposed project; Web links to relevant online materials; Needs assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are examples of materials applicants may include as supporting documentation for the proposed project (see Table of Application Components). Include relevant attachments to demonstrate prior work, specifications, planning, and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration requirements — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting an application, an applicant organization must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number; a current and active System for Award Management (SAM) registration; and an active Grants.gov registration with an approved Authorized Organization Representative (AOR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check materials and registrations well in advance of the application deadline to ensure they are accurate, current, and active.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number is a non-proprietary alphanumeric identifier assigned to all entities who register to do business with the Federal Government. The UEI has replaced the D‑U‑N‑S® Number and is requested in, and assigned by, SAM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees must inform any subrecipients that the awardee may not make a subaward unless the subrecipient has also obtained a UEI.

rubrics_metrics.name: System for Award Management (SAM) registration
rubrics_metrics.description: SAM is a federal repository that centralizes information about grant applicants and awardees. There is no fee to register with SAM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be registered with SAM before registering with Grants.gov. Allow several weeks for SAM registration. Maintain an active SAM registration with current information at all times while an award is active or an application is pending; renew at least every 12 months. An expired registration prevents submitting applications and receiving awards/payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov registration and AOR
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov is the centralized location for grant seekers to find and apply for federal funding opportunities. Applicants must register with Grants.gov prior to submitting an application package. The multistep registration process generally cannot be completed in a single day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow several weeks to complete the Grants.gov registration. The Grants.gov user ID and password are required to submit. Create an Organizational Applicant Profile; the EBiz POC must assign roles including the Authorized Organization Representative (AOR). Designate more than one AOR to avoid last‑minute crises and update contact information/passwords when personnel change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission dates and times / method
rubrics_metrics.description: All organizations must submit their applications for funding using Grants.gov Workspace. Do not submit through email or postal mail to IMLS. For Museums for America, Grants.gov will accept applications through 11:59 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time on November 15, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS makes grants only to eligible applicants that submit applications, including attachments, through Grants.gov, on or before the deadline as indicated by the Grants.gov date stamp. Do not wait until the deadline to register or submit. Under some circumstances, IMLS allows deadline extensions for organizations adversely affected by declared emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intergovernmental review
rubrics_metrics.description: This funding opportunity is not subject to intergovernmental review per Exec. Order No. 12372.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may use IMLS funds and cost share only for allowable costs as found in IMLS and OMB government-wide cost-principle rules (see 2 C.F.R. part 200 and 2 C.F.R. part 3187). Examples of generally allowable costs include personnel salaries, wages, and fringe benefits; travel expenses for key project staff and consultants; materials, supplies, software, and equipment related directly to project activities; adaptive and/or assistive technologies to improve accessibility; equipment to improve collections storage and exhibit environments; third‑party costs; publication design and printing; program evaluation; staff and volunteer training; paid internships/fellowships; and indirect or overhead costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must explain all proposed expenses in the Budget Justification. Consult 2 C.F.R. part 200 and 2 C.F.R. part 3187 for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unallowable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The following are examples of unallowable costs: general fundraising costs (e.g., development office staff time devoted to general fundraising), contributions to endowments, general operating support, acquisition of collections (see 2 C.F.R. § 3187.15(b)), general advertising or public relations costs designed solely for promotional activities other than those related to the specific project (see 2 C.F.R. § 200.421), construction or renovation of facilities (generally any activity involving the construction trades is not allowable) (see 20 U.S.C. § 9109), social activities/receptions/entertainment (see 2 C.F.R. § 200.438), and research projects (see 2 C.F.R. § 200.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have questions about whether specific activities are allowable, contact IMLS staff for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs for third parties (subrecipient vs contractor)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a project requires payment of federal funds to third parties (partners, consultants, collaborators, vendors, service providers), the applicant organization is responsible for determining whether a third party is a subrecipient or a contractor. The characterization must be reflected in the terms of each agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 2 C.F.R. § 200.1 for definitions and 2 C.F.R. § 200.331 for subrecipient and contractor determinations. IMLS grant funds may not be provided to any federal agency serving as a third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs options
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant can choose to: use a rate not to exceed their current indirect cost rate already negotiated with a federal agency; use an indirect cost rate proposed to a federal agency for negotiation (but not yet finalized) provided it is finalized by time of award; use a rate not to exceed 10 percent of the Modified Total Direct Costs (MTDC) if the organization does not have a Federally Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA) and is not subject to other requirements; or not include any indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click the IMLS link for further information on indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost share treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost share is an eligibility criterion and is not considered in the review of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost share requirements for this grant program are addressed in Section C2 of the Notice of Funding Opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion: Project Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate how well the proposal aligns with the selected Museums for America program goal/project category and objectives; whether the ways in which this project advances the museum’s strategic plan are specific and measurable; how well the applicant used relevant data and best practices to describe the need, problem, or challenge; whether target groups/beneficiaries are appropriately defined; whether target groups and stakeholders were involved in planning; and for Collections Stewardship and Access projects, whether the collections/records and their current condition are described and quantified in enough detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider Required, Conditionally Required, and Supporting Documents listed in Section D2a. Use these questions to assess the strength of the justification and connection to institutional strategy and need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion: Project Work Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate whether proposed activities are informed by relevant theory and practice; whether the goals, assumptions, and risks are clearly stated; whether identified staff, partners, consultants, and service providers possess the experience and skills necessary; whether time, financial, personnel, and other resources identified are realistic for scope and scale; whether the proposed Performance Measurement Plan is likely to generate required measures of Effectiveness, Efficiency, Quality, and Timeliness; whether the Digital Products Plan (if present) reflects appropriate practices and standards; and whether methods for tracking progress will allow course adjustments and result in reliable and measurable information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the realism and feasibility of the work plan and adequacy of staff and resources. The Performance Measurement Plan should generate required measures and permit course corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion: Project Results
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate whether the project’s intended results are clearly articulated, realistic, meaningful, and linked to the need; whether the plan to effect meaningful change in knowledge, skills, behaviors, and/or attitudes is solidly grounded and appropriately structured; whether the federal investment will generate identifiable societal benefits; whether products will be made available and accessible to the target group; whether the plan to sustain benefits beyond the period of performance is reasonable and practical; and for Collections Stewardship and Access projects, whether care, condition, management, access to, or use of museum collections/records will improve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity, practicality, potential impact, accessibility of products, and sustainability plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and selection process (peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS uses a peer review process to evaluate all complete applications from eligible institutions. Reviewers are professionals in the field with relevant knowledge and expertise. Peer reviewers must comply with IMLS’s federal ethics and conflicts of interest requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director considers peer review input and makes final funding decisions consistent with agency mission and program purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Integrity and Performance System (risk review for awards over threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to making a federal award with a total federal amount greater than the simplified acquisition threshold (currently $250,000 but periodically adjusted), IMLS is required to review and consider information about the applicant in the designated integrity and performance system accessible through SAM (41 U.S.C. § 2313 and 41 U.S.C. § 134).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may review information in the system and comment on any information about itself. IMLS will consider applicant comments and other information when completing the review of risk posed by applicants (see 2 C.F.R. § 200.206).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated announcement and award dates
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS will not release information about the status of an application until applications have been reviewed and deliberations concluded. IMLS expects to notify both successful and unsuccessful applicants by email in August 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS will notify by email; do not expect public status updates until review is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal award administrative and national policy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations that receive IMLS grants or cooperative agreements are subject to 2 C.F.R. part 200 Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards, 2 C.F.R. part 3187, the IMLS General Terms and Conditions for IMLS Discretionary Grant and Cooperative Agreement Awards, and the IMLS Assurances and Certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be familiar with these requirements and comply with applicable law. Failure to comply may result in suspension/termination of an award and require return of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must submit interim and final financial and performance reports according to the reporting schedule in the official award notification, using the IMLS electronic grants management system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim and final performance reports may be made accessible on the IMLS website. Awardees must comply with reporting related to debarment/suspension and, if federal share > $500,000 over the period of performance, refer to 2 C.F.R. part 200, Appendix XII and mandatory disclosures (see 2 C.F.R. §§ 200.113 and 200.211(c)(1)(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledging IMLS support
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must include an acknowledgement of IMLS support in all grant products, publications, websites, and presentations developed with IMLS funding and include the associated grant award number(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Grantee Communications Kit for guidance on fulfilling these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of information in applications
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS may share grant applications, products, and reports to further the agency mission and development of services. As a general practice, and except for privacy-protected information, information contained in IMLS applications that receive funding may be made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any information you deem confidential and/or proprietary and seek to have protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest requirements (awardees)
rubrics_metrics.description: As non-federal entities, awardees must follow IMLS conflict of interest policies for federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click IMLS link for more information about conflict of interest requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and federal use rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees may copyright any work developed under an award or acquired under a federal award. IMLS reserves a royalty-free, nonexclusive, and irrevocable right to reproduce, publish, or otherwise use the work for federal purposes, and to authorize others to do so (see 2 C.F.R. § 200.315).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurances: Financial, administrative, and legal accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorized representative certifies that the applicant has legal authority to apply and the institutional, managerial, and financial capability (including funds sufficient to pay non-federal share) to ensure proper planning, management, reporting, recordkeeping, and completion of the project. The applicant will cause required financial and compliance audits to be performed and will comply with applicable OMB circulars and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authorized representative signs these assurances on SF-424S and they obligate the applicant for the period of federal assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorized representative certifies compliance with nondiscrimination statutes and implementing regulations, including: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (race, color, national origin) (and Exec. Order 13166 on LEP access), Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (disability), Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 (sex in education programs), the Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1975 (age), and any other applicable nondiscrimination statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS applies regulations (e.g., 45 C.F.R. part 1181) for Section 504 compliance and requires reasonable steps to ensure LEP persons have meaningful access to programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debarment and suspension certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall comply with 2 C.F.R. part 3185 and 2 C.F.R. part 180. The authorized representative certifies that, to the best of their knowledge and belief, neither the applicant nor any of its principals are presently excluded or disqualified; have been convicted within the preceding three years of listed offenses; are presently indicted or charged with such offenses; or have had public transactions terminated for cause or default within the preceding three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unable to certify, attach an explanation. Primary tier participants must comply with 2 C.F.R. part 180 (Subpart C) and must communicate compliance requirements to next lower tier participants in covered transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal debt status certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorized representative certifies to the best of their knowledge that the applicant is not delinquent in the repayment of any federal debt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug-free workplace certification
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of the award, the applicant certifies that it will provide a drug-free workplace by complying with requirements in 2 C.F.R. part 3186 (which adopts government-wide implementation in 2 C.F.R. part 182).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include making a good faith effort to maintain a drug-free workplace, publishing a drug-free workplace statement, establishing a drug-free awareness program, taking actions concerning employees convicted of workplace drug offenses, and identifying known workplaces under federal awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trafficking in persons certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorized representative certifies, as a condition of the award, that the applicant will comply with trafficking in persons requirements set out in the General Terms and Conditions for IMLS Discretionary Awards (2 C.F.R. § 175.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding lobbying activities (applicants requesting > $100,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorized representative certifies that no federal appropriated funds have been paid or will be paid to influence federal officials in connection with awarding federal contracts/grants/agreements. If non-federal funds have been used for such lobbying, the applicant must complete and submit Standard Form LLL 'Disclosure of Lobbying Activities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification must be included in award documents for all subawards at all tiers. Failure to file required certification may result in civil penalties of $10,000 to $100,000 per failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: General certification (other federal requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorized representative certifies that the applicant will comply with all applicable requirements of all other federal laws, executive orders, regulations, and policies governing the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subawards — authorization and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under IMLS regulations (2 C.F.R. § 3187.14), a recipient may not make a subaward unless expressly authorized by IMLS. A recipient may contract for supplies, equipment, and services subject to applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients who plan to use awards to fund contracts must comply with communication and verification requirements in Debarment and Suspension provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native American human remains and associated funerary objects (NAGPRA) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorized representative certifies that the applicant will comply with the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act of 1990 (25 U.S.C. § 3001 et seq.) if the organization controls or possesses Native American human remains, associated funerary objects and/or cultural items and receives federal funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic properties / Section 106 compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorized representative certifies that the applicant will assist the awarding agency in ensuring compliance with Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act of 1966, Exec. Order No. 11593, and related preservation laws as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental protections compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorized representative certifies that the project will comply with environmental standards including: (a) instituting environmental quality control measures under NEPA and Exec. Order No. 11514; (b) notification of violating facilities pursuant to Exec. Order No. 11738; (c) protection of wetlands pursuant to Exec. Order No. 11990 (as amended); (d) evaluation of flood hazards in floodplains per Exec. Order No. 11988 (as amended); (e) assurance of project consistency with approved state Coastal Zone Management program; (f) the Clean Air Act; (g) protection of underground sources of drinking water under the Safe Drinking Water Act; and (h) protection of endangered species under the Endangered Species Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes compliance with the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act and Flood Disaster Protection Act (flood insurance purchase requirements for projects in special flood hazard areas when insurable construction/acquisition >= $10,000 or as designated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research on human subjects compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorized representative certifies that the project will comply with 45 C.F.R. part 46 regarding the protection of human subjects involved in research, development, and related activities supported by the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research on animal subjects compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorized representative certifies that the project will comply with the Animal Welfare Act of 1966, as amended (7 U.S.C. § 2131 et seq.) pertaining to care, handling, and treatment of warm-blooded animals held for research, teaching, or other activities supported by the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for acquiring a UEI (Appendix Two)
rubrics_metrics.description: The UEI has replaced the D‑U‑N‑S® Number and is requested in, and assigned by, SAM. Applicants with active SAM registrations can find their assigned UEI; applicants without active SAM registrations will receive a UEI when they register in SAM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For more information visit gsa.gov/entityid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for registering with SAM (Appendix Two)
rubrics_metrics.description: SAM centralizes information about grant applicants and awardees and is free. Applicants must register with SAM before registering with Grants.gov. Representatives must create a SAM user account through Login.gov then proceed to SAM registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow several weeks to complete SAM registration. Maintain active SAM registration and update within 12 months or when information changes. Grant payments will be made to the bank account associated with the organization's SAM registration. An expired registration will prevent application submission and award/payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for registering with Grants.gov and using Workspace (Appendix Two)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov is free; applicants must register with Grants.gov before submitting an application. After registering and creating an Organizational Applicant Profile, the EBiz POC assigns roles including the AOR. Workspace is a shared online environment where team members can simultaneously access and edit forms and create copies of a workspace for each funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow several weeks for Grants.gov registration. Click Grants.gov Support or call Applicant Support for assistance. Use multiple AORs and keep contact information/passwords updated.
